newsitem.title: UK: UK gas user complaints in second pilot area pour in.
newsitem.headline: UK gas user complaints in second pilot area pour in.

text.p: Centrica plc's British Gas Trading (BGT) has received 200 complaints over selling techniques in the second pilot area for domestic gas deregulation in Soutwest England since the launch of the pilot nine days ago, a spokesman for the company said on Wednesday.
So far around 13,500 customers in the second pilot area, covering Dorset and the former county of Avon, have left the former British Gas, now split into Centrica and BG plc.
"We have started feeding these complaints through to the Gas Consumers' Council (GCC)," said the BGT spokesman. "But we have known since the end of last year that the complaints were coming."
Some of the newly-licensed suppliers in the second pilot area have been claiming to potential customers that BGT will no longer be supplying their area, he added.
Some customers were also told they would have to sign up with new suppliers if they were to continue receiving gas at all, he said.

On learning that a customer has left, BGT sends a "farewell letter." It is this which has led to the complaint, as some customers have said they were not aware of having left BGT or of signing anything.
In some cases, according to BGT, customers thought they had only signed a form requesting further information.
When the first pilot area, covering Devon, Cornwall and Somerset, was opened to competition on April 29 last year, British Gas received 3,000 similar letters of complaint.
Another pilot area covering Kent and East and West Sussex opens for competition on March 7, and the whole country will open for competition during 1998.
